emergencyGuidelines.title: Adult & Pediatric CPR
emergencyGuidelines.summary: Immediate life support for unresponsive victims not breathing normally.
steps: Check scene safety: Ensure no live electrical wires, toxic fumes, or structural collapse danger.
Check responsiveness: Tap victim's collarbone firmly and shout 'Can you hear me?'.
Check breathing for 10 seconds: Look for chest rise. If absent or agonal gasping, begin CPR.
Hand placement: Place heel of one hand in center of victim's chest (lower half of breastbone), interlock other hand fingers.
Compressions: Push hard and fast at 100-120 beats/min (to rhythm of 'Stayin' Alive'). Depth: 5 to 6 cm (2 inches). Allow full chest recoil.
Cycle: 30 hard compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths (tilt head back, pinch nose, seal mouth). If untrained, perform continuous hands-only CPR.
proTips: Do not stop CPR until AED arrives, victim starts moving, or responder is physically exhausted.
Switch compressor every 2 minutes to prevent compression fatigue.

emergencyGuidelines.title: Arterial Bleeding & Tourniquet
emergencyGuidelines.summary: Life-saving technique for severe spurting or pooling limb hemorrhage.
steps: Expose the wound: Cut or tear clothing to identify the exact origin of bleeding.
Direct pressure: Pack wound with clean gauze or cloth and apply direct two-handed bodyweight pressure.
If bleeding does not stop immediately: Apply emergency commercial tourniquet or improvised windlass 5-7 cm (2-3 inches) ABOVE wound (never directly over a joint).
Tighten strap until snug, then turn windlass rod until bright red arterial bleeding stops and distal pulse vanishes.
Lock windlass in clip and write exact time of application (e.g. 'T-14:22') on victim's forehead or tourniquet label.
proTips: NEVER loosen or remove a tourniquet once applied in the field—only qualified surgical staff should release it.
Pain is normal; an effective tourniquet is extremely tight.

emergencyGuidelines.title: Building Collapse & Rubble Entrapment
emergencyGuidelines.summary: Techniques for surviving while trapped under structural rubble and concrete debris.
steps: Protect airways: Cover mouth and nose with cloth, shirt, or mask to prevent fatal dust and silica inhalation.
Do not panic or yell continuously: Shouting consumes precious oxygen and accelerates dehydration and dust inhalation.
Create survival pocket: If moving is possible, tuck into fetal position against rigid load-bearing furniture or solid structural pillars ('Triangle of Life').
Acoustic signaling: Tap rhythmically with a metal object, stone, or pipe in bursts of 3 (Universal SOS: TAP-TAP-TAP ... pause ... TAP-TAP-TAP) whenever hearing rescue equipment.
Conserve battery: Keep phone in battery-saver mode. Turn off non-essential wireless radios except BLE beacon.
proTips: Rescuers stop machinery every 30 minutes for silence checks. Tap continuously when silence is heard.

emergencyGuidelines.title: Rising Floodwater Evacuation & Water Safety
emergencyGuidelines.summary: Protocols for escaping flash floods, urban inundation, and storm surges.
steps: Cut primary utilities: Switch off main electrical circuit breaker and gas line before water reaches electrical sockets.
Never enter moving water: As little as 15 cm (6 inches) of rapid water can knock an adult off their feet; 60 cm (2 feet) floats SUVs.
Vertical evacuation: Move to the highest accessible floor. Take water, emergency documents, and beacon.
Avoid attic traps: NEVER climb into a closed attic without an axe or roof escape hatch; trapped individuals can drown as water levels peak.
Submerged vehicle escape: Open window immediately before pressure equalization locks door. If jammed, break side window using pointed tool at glass corner.
proTips: Floodwater carries dangerous sewage, chemical runoff, and submerged debris. Treat cuts immediately with antiseptic.

emergencyGuidelines.title: Emergency Water Purification
emergencyGuidelines.summary: Generating safe drinking water from contaminated surface sources.
steps: Pre-filtration: Pour murky water through a folded clean cotton cloth or bandanna to remove silt and particulates.
Boiling (Gold Standard): Bring water to a vigorous rolling boil for at least 1 full minute (3 minutes at high altitude).

Disinfection with Unscented Household Bleach: Add 2 drops of standard 6-8% household bleach per 1 Liter of clear water (4 drops if cloudy). Mix and wait 30 minutes. Water should have faint chlorine odor.
Solar SODIS Method: Fill clear PET plastic bottles and place in direct sunlight on metal roof for minimum 6 hours to deactivate pathogens via UV.
proTips: Never drink floodwater, radiator fluid, or seawater under any circumstances.

emergencyGuidelines.title: Severe Hypothermia & Cold Shock
emergencyGuidelines.summary: Preventing and reversing core body temperature drop in wet, flooded environments.
steps: Remove wet clothing: Strip soaked fabric immediately and replace with dry blankets, space foil sheets, or dry layers.
Insulate from ground: Lay victim on waterproof tarp, cardboard, or foliage—direct ground contact leaches body heat rapidly.
Rewarm the core first: Apply warm compress or skin-to-skin contact to chest, neck, and groin (never extremities first, which causes cold-blood heart shock).
Do not rub frostbitten limbs: Vigorous friction causes permanent tissue damage.
proTips: Provide warm sweetened broth or water only if the victim is fully conscious and capable of swallowing.
